extracted.intended_audience: researchers or analysts studying patent-practice survey data (patent attorneys, policymakers, IP scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction/analysis of tabular survey results showing how patent practice types and patent-origin (jurisdiction/source of priority) are distributed across respondents and filings. The page contains multiple tables breaking down practice type, filing origin, prior filings, and respondent counts/percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Practice by Origin of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: (appears as a table heading) Breaks down respondents' practice types by the origin of patentability (e.g., US utility patents vs. other origins). The table lists counts/percentages by practice categories and by where the patentability originated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare how different practice types (prosecution, litigation, transactional, counseling, etc.) are distributed depending on the jurisdiction/source of the patent filing. Contains numeric counts and percent columns; use caution interpreting OCR-numbered cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice Type by Respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: (label repeated in document) Classification of respondents according to their patent-practice type (e.g., filing for ready devices, computer/technology, chemical/mechanical/biotech/life, complex/real property?). The item lists respondent counts and percentages for each practice-type category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the key categorical breakdown of survey participants. Categories appear in prose and abbreviated codes (OCRed); verify original table for exact category labels when using this data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent application with prior filing from (foreign/prior jurisdiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether patent applications handled by respondents had a prior filing in another jurisdiction (i.e., filings with prior foreign or domestic priority). Appears in headings such as 'Patent application with prior filing from ...' or 'filing with prior filing from'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for measuring cross‑jurisdiction priority filings (PCT/Paris Convention follow-ons). The table supplies counts and percentages of applications that had prior filings; OCR noise may have split headings—consult source table for precise jurisdiction labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location by Origin of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: (table heading) Geographic/location breakdown of patent filings by the origin of patentability (regions such as West, South, East, other). Shows counts/percentages of filings/respondents by geographic region tied to origin of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables regional analysis of where inventions originate versus where filings are prosecuted. Regions appear as abbreviated labels in the OCR; map them back to original region names for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent counts, percentages, and summary statistics (Mean, Quality metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables include summary measures: number of responses, percent columns, mean values and a 'Quality' metric (OCRed as 'Quality tsriF' or similar). These give summary statistics across the categorical breakdowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the numeric basis for inference (n, % and mean). Because OCR has distorted some labels and numbers, confirm numeric values with original PDF tables before reporting or statistical testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice-type-specific filing categories (examples appearing in table body)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific filing-category labels appearing in table cells, e.g., 'filing for ready device', 'filing for computer/technology', 'filing for chemical/mechanical/biotech/life', 'complex/real', and 'filing with prior from PCT/non-US/US' (as shown in various rows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These row labels represent the subject-matter or filing-format categories used to disaggregate the survey. OCR corruption is present — recover exact category text from source to ensure accurate category mapping.
